en: break the crust of a cassoulet

does: Presses the golden crust that forms on top of a slowly baked pot of beans and meat down into the pot, so that it soaks up the juices and thickens them, then lets a fresh crust form. It is done several times, and the last crust is left whole for the table.

intro.what: A browned crust on a bean pot is pressed into the juices before a fresh crust forms.
intro.why: This repeated movement makes the surface part of the thickened interior while preserving a final crisp top.

how: Sprinkle a thick layer of crumbs over the beans and meat, with the liquid just below the top.
Bake at a low heat until a golden crust has formed on the top.
Press the crust down into the pot with the back of a spoon so that it sinks into the juices. If the pot looks dry, add a ladle of hot liquid.
Sprinkle on a little more crumbs if the top is bare, and bake until a fresh crust forms.
Do this several times over the baking. Leave the last crust whole.

cues.text: A deep golden crust, thicker than a gratin, with the beans below it glossy and moist.
The spoon cracks through a crisp top into a thick, creamy mass of beans.

mistakes.mistake: Breaking the crust before it has browned, so that the crumbs turn to a paste and it never forms again.
mistakes.fix: Wait for a golden crust before each press.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the pot dry out under the crust.
mistakes.fix: Add a ladle of hot liquid whenever the beans no longer shine.

quiz.question: Why press a formed crust into the bean pot?
choices: It absorbs juices and helps thicken them.
It keeps the crumbs permanently separate from the sauce.
It keeps a permanent dry lid above the beans.
quiz.because: The submerged crust takes up liquid and becomes part of the thickened beans.

quiz.question: When should the crust be pressed down?
choices: While the crumbs are still pale and damp.
Only after the pot has dried out.
quiz.because: The crust needs to form before it can be broken into the juices.

quiz.question: What contrast should the spoon encounter?
choices: A wet loose topping above dry beans.
A burnt surface above thin clear water.
A crisp surface above creamy moist beans.
quiz.because: The method combines a browned top with a thick, moist interior.

quiz.question: Pale crumbs become paste and no new crust forms. What should change?
choices: Wait for browning before pressing them down.
Press the pale crumbs down sooner.
quiz.because: Waiting lets a proper crust develop before it meets the liquid.

variant_of.differs: A gratin is browned once under strong heat from above and eaten at once. Here the crust is pressed down into the pot several times during a long, low bake, so that it thickens the beans and a new crust takes its place.
